prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Mungoon-Gali, the enormous venomous ancestral goanna of Yuwaalaraay tradition.
ANATOMY: ONE GIANT Australian GOANNA/MONITOR LIZARD, one long wedge-shaped reptilian head, TWO natural dark eyes, FOUR muscular sprawled reptile LEGS and FOUR clawed feet, ONE long thick tapering tail. Rough dark brown and ochre mottled scales, long forked tongue, natural small pointed monitor teeth; no horns, dorsal sail, wings, crocodile body or extra limbs [mungoon-gali-c01,mungoon-gali-c05].
MOMENT: Scramble down a rocky ledge toward viewer, body seen THREE-QUARTER SIDE so all FOUR legs and FOUR feet distinct: two front paws braced wide foreground, two rear paws staggered behind to the right, tail curves into background. Head leans low toward camera with mouth open in warning and forked tongue extended, physical dust lifts beneath claws.
POWER: venomous bite capability in ancestral time, no visible toxin clouds or venom beams, no victim or biting contact [mungoon-gali-c01].
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme ground-level low close angle; huge goanna head/body dominate, one tiny EMPTY adult-sized bark shelter in background shows ancestral giant size, no people. This is great ancestral form, not present dwarfed five-foot form [mungoon-gali-c05].
LIGHT & WEATHER: one low amber sunset rims coarse scales and forked tongue, deep walnut rock shadows, ordinary airborne dust and dry leaf litter.
SURFACE: rough pebbled brown-ochre monitor scales, curved claws, dry bark and red-brown stone.
SETTING: editorial Australian dry eucalyptus woodland and rocky ledge, no sacred art motifs or named site invented.
MOOD: awe-inspiring dangerous ancestral reptile through documented size and bodily presence, never ordinary pet lizard, cute, static or decorative.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. Premium painterly brushwork, dark warm walnut and antique gold palette, square composition.
name: Mungoon-Gali
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px inspected: one giant goanna with wedge head/two eyes/forked tongue, exactly four sprawled legs (two foreground, rear right, rear left over ledge), one long tapering tail, no sail/horns. Empty shelter and trees set giant ancestral scale, active downward scramble/dust and open natural mouth remain imposing at 200px. No visible venom mist, sacred motifs, text, victims or aura. Seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and head, all-feet, upper-left-limb and rear-leg/tail crops. One giant goanna (mungoon-gali-c01) with one wedge-shaped monitor head, eyes in three-quarter view (one visible), small pointed teeth, and a long forked tongue flicking from a gaping mouth. Its rough, dark, ochre-speckled scales follow Australian monitor anatomy. Legs: two massive front legs plant in the foreground, each foot with five curved claws, and one rear leg steps down beside the tail. The remaining sprawled limb arches over the rock at the upper left, partly hidden, and no fifth foot can be read. It has one long tapering tail. The giant size (an ancestral form larger than today's five-foot goanna, c01/c05) shows against an empty bark shelter that it dwarfs, with no people. It scrambles down a red rock ledge straight at a ground-level camera, kicking up dust. The venomous bite (c01) is implied only by the open mouth, with no venom mist or victims. Dry eucalyptus country at sunset under one low sun, with no invented sacred motifs and no text. It dominates the frame and stays dangerous at 200px.
